scenario: A mobile app review platform only features apps that have exceeded 10,000 downloads, treating smaller apps as insufficiently validated. A product manager uses the platform's average download count to set launch targets for new apps.

data.description: Platform features only apps with > 10,000 downloads. Download counts assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = 8,000.

question: Featured apps average 22,000 downloads. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean download count Î¼ across ALL apps launched (including those never featured), and (b) the fraction of all apps that get featured.
naive_answer: The typical app gets about 22,000 downloads since that is the platform average.
naive_trap: About 9% of launched apps never reach 10,000 downloads and are excluded. The true mean is 20,500 â€” 1,500 lower. Setting launch targets based on 22,000 benchmarks the lower bound against featured apps, which is a survivorship-inflated figure.

python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(10-mu)/8; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+8*norm.pdf(a)/sf-22 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,20,21)
assert abs(mu-20.514)<0.25
